            Added — HTTP Observatory: grade every published site, see who caused each finding, fix it on the FortiWeb (2026-10-16)

            • New page Troubleshooting › HTTP Observatory (Global, FortiWeb and FortiADC ADOMs). Operator request: "a tool like the MDN HTTP Observatory". Every FortiWeb server policy and FortiADC virtual server is listed with its VIP, its HTTP/HTTPS ports and a site name (Host/SNI, the first Protected Hostname by default); Grade or Grade all scores them with the MDN HTTP Observatory's twelve tests and scoring (algorithm version 6). Checked against the MDN API: developer.mozilla.org and example.com get the same score in both; a preloaded site gets 5 points less here because the HSTS preload list is not consulted (stated on the page).
            • SATOM connects only to the policy's VIP, on the ports the policy serves; a redirect is followed only while it stays on the policy. An untrusted certificate is a graded finding, and the summary shows the grade the site would get with a trusted one.
            • Each test says who produced the result — FortiWeb (HTTP Header Security profile, HSTS or redirect on the server policy, its own cookiesession1 cookie), the application, or the certificate — read from the appliance's configuration.
            • Fix on the FortiWeb (config_write): tick fixes, preview the writes, the server policies they reach and the projected grade, then apply. Header rows (X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, a starter Content-Security-Policy, and Cross-Origin-Resource/Opener/Embedder-Policy on builds that accept them, per the API library), HSTS, HTTP-to-HTTPS, FortiWeb's own cookie flags and Cookie Security flags for the application's cookies. Writes go through the object editor's path (re-read verification, change history); template-managed profiles, another user's edit lease and values that would not pass are refused before anything is sent, and a change that reaches other server policies names them and needs a confirmation. The site is graded again after the fix. Every fix was measured on FortiWeb 8.0.6 (and the payloads on 7.6.8) before it was offered.
            • History keeps 60 grades per site; the new scheduled action HTTP Observatory — grade published sites (observatory_scan) grades every site of its targets and names a lower grade first. Stored results never contain cookie values or page bodies.
            • The Transaction Tracer shows the security-header grade of leg A's response, with a link to the Observatory.

            Fixed — Published-service probes read custom services and the HTTPS service of a policy (2026-10-16)

            • The resolver behind the upgrade pre-flight service probes, Path Diagnostics and the new Observatory read custom services from service-custom, which FortiWeb 7.6.8 and 8.0.6 answer with "invalid URL", so every custom port became 80 or 443; they are read from service.custom now. It also ignored a policy's https-service, so a policy with an HTTP and an HTTPS front end was probed at https://<vip>:80/; both ports are resolved now and the HTTPS one is preferred.

            Added — Transaction Tracer: a page with cookie analysis, revealable values and a HAR viewer (2026-10-16)

            • The transaction tracer moved out of the header Tools menu into Operations › Troubleshooting › Transaction Tracer, in every ADOM. It is a page now: the trace, its cookies and its HAR stay on screen, and ?vip=, ?backend= and ?path= prefill the form.
            • Cookies for each leg: every cookie the response sets with its flags, the cookies the request sent, and what a browser will do with them (rejected for SameSite=None without Secure or a broken __Host-/__Secure- prefix, warnings for a missing Secure or HttpOnly). With both legs, Cookies A vs C names the cookies the appliance issued, removed or rewrote.
            • Reveal values (new permission monitoring.reveal_secrets, Administrator-only): shows the real cookie, Authorization and API-key values in the page. They are never written to the audit log, which records only that values were revealed; trace answers are no longer cacheable.
            • HAR viewer: the trace's HAR, or any HAR file you open (read in the browser, never uploaded), as a table with a waterfall and per-entry headers, cookies, timings and content. The exported HAR now carries each leg's real start time, server address, query string and structured cookies; values and the response body are included only on request, with the new permission, and that export is audited.
            • Each leg also shows the request headers it sent and the first 2,000 characters of the response body.

            Fixed — Transaction Tracer: a cookie the appliance rewrites is no longer called "identical" (2026-10-16)

            • Set-Cookie values are compared by their redacted length, so an appliance that added Secure to a cookie of the same length produced the verdict the appliance is not altering this transaction. Cookie flags are now compared directly and a rewritten cookie makes the verdict transforming.

            Fixed — Concept Map: the newest pages are findable by what they do (2026-10-16)

            • The map's coverage check failed after three JSON endpoints shipped without an entry: the server hints behind Fetch… on WAF Artifacts and the two database-lookup catalogs of the Script Library form designer. They are now listed as JSON feeds, so the map again accounts for every page in the console (122 pages on the map and 154 written exclusions today).
            • Search now reaches the features added on 2026-10-15: fetch, wsdl, soap or import finds Artifact inventory; adom, confine or restrict finds Permission Profiles; compare, lookup, dataset or query builder finds Script Library.

            Changed — Cert Manager: Windows renewal fields line up (2026-10-16)

            • In the Windows renewal settings the inputs share one baseline, and Auto-renew sits on its own line under them instead of floating beside the last field.

            Fixed — Cert Manager: Copy on a certificate signing request works (2026-10-16)

            • On a certificate's page, Copy next to a signing request generated for another CA did nothing: its script lacked the page's content-security nonce, so the browser blocked it without a message. It now copies the request.
            • The private-key boxes on New certificate and the import form keep their PEM hint, now produced when the page is drawn, so the release secret scanner no longer stops a release on the template.

            Fixed — Clone and migrate: the schemas a WSDL or XML Schema imports are created first (2026-10-15)

            • A policy clone or migration now carries the XML Schemas that a WSDL or XML Schema imports, not only the files a rule names. FortiWeb checks those imports when the file is uploaded and looks each one up as an XML Schema object already on the device, so a WSDL that arrived before its schemas was refused after everything before it had been written. Before the first write, SATOM now reads the content it is about to upload: a schema the plan already creates further down is moved ahead of the file that imports it, a schema the destination already holds is left alone, and any other one is added to the plan right before it, with the copy SATOM holds (deepest first).
            • The pre-flight lists those imported schemas and which file needs each one. A schema SATOM can't supply goes through the same acknowledgement as any other missing file; the files that import it, directly or through another schema, are then skipped instead of being refused by the device mid-run.

            Added — WAF Artifacts: fetch a WSDL or XML Schema from the application (2026-10-15)

            • Fetch from the application (WAF Artifacts → Inventory) brings in the WSDL and XML Schema files of a FortiWeb already in production. The device won't return those two types, but the SOAP service it protects usually publishes them (often at its address followed by ?wsdl). SATOM downloads the document, follows the XML Schema and WSDL import, include and redefine references on the same host, and stores each document as a new version with the origin fetched and the URL in its note. The first document takes the object name you give (use the one the policy already references); imported schemas are named after their file. Touches no appliance. Requested by the operator: "we need a way to integrate FortiWebs that are already in use".
            • Safe by construction: http/https only, no credentials in the URL, redirects reported instead of followed, references to another host listed and not fetched, documents with a DTD or entity declarations refused, and at most 25 documents, 5 levels and 60 seconds. Loopback, link-local and the node's own addresses are refused before connecting and again on the connected socket, so a host name that changes what it resolves to between the two checks is still caught.
            • References are rewritten to the stored object names. Measured on FortiWeb 7.6.8: the device checks a schema's schemaLocation when the file is uploaded, and opens a relative one as an XML Schema object on the device, by name. A copy kept exactly as served (types/order.xsd, OrderService?xsd=1) is refused, so each followed reference now names the object it was stored as, and the version note says so. A reference SATOM did not fetch is left as written and listed: the device resolves it itself (it downloads an absolute URL at upload time) and refuses the file if it can't. soap:address is never touched.
            • The Origin filter on the inventory has a fetched option.
            • In Needed by a policy and NOT held, an XML Schema or WSDL row now reads no — fetch or upload and has a Fetch… button: the dialog opens with the object name filled in and offers, as starting URLs, the real servers behind the policies that use it (read from the device when you open it, not on page load).
            • A refused XML Schema, WSDL or other file upload now shows the device's own reason (for example Cannot open '/data/etc/xml_schema/root/x.xsd' to retrieve schema) instead of a bare HTTP 500: FortiWeb sends it in errmsg, without an error code.

            Added — Script Library: form fields fed from the SATOM database (2026-10-15)

            • Three new field types: lookup (pick one row), lookup_multi (pick several) and dataset (the whole result goes to the script). Each one has a query built in the form designer: a table, other tables combined with it (only the related ones are offered, with the join explained, up to two joins away), columns, filters, order and a row limit, plus which column is the value and which the label. Preview rows runs it at once.
            • The script never touches the database: SATOM runs the query (read-only, from the Report Builder catalogue; credential columns and tables are refused) and passes the rows on standard input — inputs["device"]["row"]["appliances.host"].
            • The rows are read with the ADOMs of whoever the run is for, and when the run is queued: a saved run reads them with its owner's ADOMs every time it fires, and a value that is no longer there fails the run instead of running on a stale copy.

            Added — Profiles can be confined to some ADOMs (2026-10-15)

            • Requested as: "if a user only has permission for one ADOM it must be only that one; if they have global permissions they can have everything". Until now an ADOM was only a view: any user could switch to Global and see the whole fleet.
            • A profile's new ADOMs card lists the ADOMs it may work in (none ticked = every ADOM, as before). A confined profile sees only those ADOMs in the switcher; opening another is refused; its Global console is the union of its ADOMs (devices, records, jobs, change requests, Sentinel, certificates, reports, metrics, dashboard tiles). Raw SQL (database browser, SQL console, DB reports) and Global ADOM Assets are refused to it, because they cannot be narrowed to an ADOM.
            • A confined administrator cannot create, widen or assign an unconfined profile, nor reset the password or clear the 2FA of an account wider than itself.

            Fixed — pages that loaded another ADOM's record by its id (2026-10-15)

            • Found while building the ADOM confinement: several pages filtered their list by ADOM but loaded a record by id without checking it, so a record the list hid was one URL away. Now 404, like the list: Certificate Manager (detail, CSR, deploy, swap, renew, revoke, delete, revocation confirm, on-device certificate swap/remove), Sentinel (incident actions, border maps, topology, blocklist release), configuration templates and provisioning baselines (every by-id route), attaching a member to an HA cluster, and ADOM Assets file listing.
            • Sentinel showed every incident in the fleet to a session that could see no FortiWeb at all, and a sweep with no device picked read the whole fleet; it now sweeps the devices the session can see.
            • The Report Builder's list of related tables phrased a join walked against its foreign key backwards ("each Appliances row belongs to one Server Policies"); it now reads in the key's direction. The Script Library query builder uses the same list.
            • Template details listed bindings on other ADOMs' devices; WAF Artifacts named other ADOMs' devices in its labels and divergence report; System Backup's coverage matrix, the firmware page's device banner and the Global dashboard's job and certificate counts read the whole fleet.

            Changed — the alert webhook secret follows the vault mode (2026-10-15)

            • The HMAC secret of the alert webhook was the last credential kept only in the SATOM database. With the vault as the only store it now lives at <mount>/alerts/webhook; in mirror mode both copies; without a vault, encrypted locally as before. Settings → Vault migrate and scrub cover it.

            Fixed — Libraries: a driver that imports but cannot connect is rolled back (2026-10-15)

            • After installing a library, the runner now opens one database connection (SELECT 1) through the new code before restarting anything. The import check alone passed psycopg 3.3.6 with psycopg-binary 3.3.4, which failed on every connection and took both nodes down.

            Fixed — the bookmarks tab covered buttons at the top right (2026-10-15)

            • The closed bookmarks rail keeps a 34 px tab on the right edge, which sat on top of page-header buttons (Script Library's Publish was the reported case). The page now reserves that strip.

            Fixed — WAF Artifacts: what a FortiWeb backup holds, and the gRPC IDL error on 8.0.6 (2026-10-15)

            • The WAF Artifacts pages said XML Schema, WSDL and gRPC IDL are absent from the device's own backup. They are not: FortiWeb's Entire configuration backup carries them, inside a block the firmware encrypts even without a backup password (measured on 7.6.8 and 8.0.6: deleting one XSD and one WSDL shrinks it by about 1.1 KB). The pages now say so, and say what follows: a restore of that backup does not bring them back. Measured on 7.6.8 → 8.0.6, 8.0.6 → 8.0.6 and 7.6.8 → 7.6.8, with a marker object proving each restore applied: the configuration comes back and every XML Schema and WSDL object is dropped, name included. A copy held in SATOM is the only way to move them.
            • A gRPC IDL upload refused with -3000 now says what was measured: FortiWeb 8.0.6 build0116 refuses every gRPC IDL upload, whatever the content or format, through SATOM's API path and through the GUI's own session path, while 7.6.8 accepts the same file: the cause is the firmware. The device's own error stays first.

            Added — Script Library: every edit is a new version, autosave, compare any two versions (2026-10-15)

            • Every edit is a new version: each save, upload and restore of a script — published or not — is recorded automatically as version vN with its code, form and settings (Versions & runs). Saves by the same person within ten minutes are grouped into one version; a save that changes nothing adds nothing; the starter template is not a version, so the first save is v1. Publish approves the latest version under its own number, and operators keep running the published one while you edit. The last 100 versions are kept, and the published one always is. Before, a save overwrote the draft and only Publish kept a copy, under a separate numbering.
            • The editor saves by itself a few seconds after the last change, and an upload is saved at once (it used to wait in the editor until Save).
            • Compare versions: pick any two in the Versions card, or compare a row with the previous version; a line diff per file and the settings that changed. View shows any version read-only; Restore saves an old version's content as a new version (nothing is deleted). Each one downloads as a zip.
            • Library page in the SATOM list layout: the standard table with a search box and row actions (edit, compare, versions, download), New script as a button that opens a dialog, and the "how scripts run" notes as one strip at the top (operator requests: "I must be able to find the script, see it and edit it online, or upload a new version, and the system must save the version automatically"; "editing a published script generates the new version; versions can be compared with an action").

            Changed — integration hook secrets follow the vault mode (2026-10-15)

            • Hook secrets were always stored encrypted in the SATOM database, even with a vault configured. They now follow Settings > Vault like appliance passwords and directory secrets: vault only (<mount>/hooks/<NAME>, the database keeps only a marker), both (vault plus an encrypted local fallback), or local when no vault is configured. The hook page says where values live.
            • Migrate existing credentials and Remove local copies include hook secrets; a local copy is removed only after the vault copy is read back and matches. Deleting a secret deletes its vault copy.
            • A run whose secret cannot be read from the vault now says so, instead of reporting the secret as not configured (operator request: "move the secrets").

            Added — Studio > Script Library: Python scripts with a form, tested and published by administrators (2026-10-15)

            • Administrators keep Python scripts as small projects (main.py plus modules and data files; upload a .py or a .zip, download any version as a zip) in an editor with a file tree, line numbers, indentation keys, Ctrl+S and a syntax check that points at the file and line.
            • A form designer defines the fields operators fill in (text, textarea, number, select, checkbox, password), with a live preview. Values reach the script typed, through satom_script.inputs; only defined fields get through. Password values are masked in every run record, output and result.
            • Test runs of the draft, publishing frozen versions (code, form, network, timeout), restoring a version to the draft, and a run history with output, result() and every connection attempt (operator request: "a place where the administrator can upload Python scripts, give them a user and password, and build a mini form for the user to fill in, like a mini IDE").
            • Runs execute in the new satom-scripts.service, which has no database connection and no access to the encryption key, inside the same bubblewrap jail as integration hooks. Network is off unless the script is set to outbound, and outbound never reaches the node itself.
            • Credentials in the vault. A script declares the credentials it needs (user + password, or a single value) and reads them with satom_script.secret("NAME"). Values are stored only in the configured vault, are write-only from the page and are masked in every run record. A queued run carries single-use wrapped tokens, never the secret; the runner unwraps them with no vault login of its own, and a token someone else used first fails the run visibly. Without a vault, credentials are unavailable (operator request: "there may be passwords, so they must be stored, not in the same database as SATOM").
            • Operations > Automation > Scripts (operators, operations.scripts_run): the published scripts offered to operators, with their form, Run now and the result. Saved runs keep a set of values on a cron schedule, pinned to the version they were created against ("move to vN" re-checks the values first). Password values of a saved run are kept in the vault and delivered wrapped. A saved run whose owner is deactivated or loses access is paused, and a missed fire is skipped rather than replayed (operator request: "the operator sees the administrator's fields and can set a cron").

            Added — cron schedules for every automation (2026-10-15)

            • Automations (and Script Library saved runs) accept a cron expression besides once / interval / daily / weekly / monthly: five fields, ranges, lists, steps and names, evaluated in the console timezone. An expression that can never fire is refused when the form is saved.

            Fixed — a systemd unit added by an update is installed and armed by that update (2026-10-15)

            • The privileged updater copied the unit list it had read before checking out the new code, so a unit introduced by an update was only installed on the next one, without its service-account drop-in. Neither the updater nor satom execute reinstall units ever enabled a new .path or .timer, so a new queue watcher stayed off on every existing node. Both now install what the new deploy/ holds and enable a .path/.timer the first time it is installed, as the installer does. A unit that was already installed keeps the enabled state it had.
            • satom-scripts.path itself reached the standby installed but not enabled (the previous updater copied it during the switch-over). The updater arms it once, and remembers having done so, so an operator who disables it later keeps it disabled.

            Added — Settings > General > System packages (2026-10-15)

            • A card under Libraries lists the operating-system packages SATOM depends on, per node: installed, version, and whether it actually works for the service account. Today that is bubblewrap, the sandbox for operator Python. A node that does not answer is shown as unreachable, never as installed.
            • Install queues the package for the privileged updater on this node and, if chosen, on the peers. The updater uses the node's package manager (apt, dnf/yum, zypper or pacman) and then runs the sandbox check as the service account. "Installed, but namespaces are not allowed" is reported as a failure, not a success. The list is curated and install-only: the request carries a package key, never a package name or a command (operator request: "add an install in Settings, General, where the pips are, for future things too").
            • The installer and the three offline bundle builders now include bubblewrap, so new installs have it. Existing nodes get it from this card.

            Security — integration hooks run in a jail with a filtered network (2026-10-15)

            • A hook ran as the same system user as the web application, contained only by systemd. That was enough to open the SATOM database over its local socket and to read the application's encryption key from another process of the same user, which together decrypt every stored credential. No hook was configured on the nodes checked, so nothing was exploited.
            • Hooks now run inside bubblewrap with private process, user, IPC and network namespaces. Only the system libraries, the Python environment (read-only), the resolver and CA files and the hook's own work directory are visible. There is no fallback: without bubblewrap a hook is refused, not run unconfined.
            • Outbound traffic goes through a proxy that refuses this node (loopback and every address it owns) and link-local addresses. It checks the connected socket, not the name, so a name that resolves to 127.0.0.1 changes nothing. HTTP(S) clients use it unchanged; satom_sdk.tcp(host, port) opens raw TCP (SSH to an appliance) through it. Each run records every attempt.

            Changed — Libraries card changes run as a job on the server; the peer step no longer needs an open browser (2026-10-15)

            • System packages too. Installing an OS package with "all nodes" used to ask the peer at the same moment as this node, so a package that broke the service could take both nodes down together, as psycopg did. It is now the same kind of job: the peer is asked only after the install succeeded here, and both nodes' steps are in the job log (operator request: "yes, do it and test it").

            • An upgrade or rollback from Settings → Libraries is now a job in the global job dock and the Job Manager, with every step of both nodes in its log (operator request: "this process should run in the background and create a job to show its status; we cannot depend on the browser for processes to run"). Before, with "also the peer" ticked, the card's JavaScript waited for this node to succeed and then asked the server to contact the peer. Closing the page left the peer untouched, and nothing reported it.

            • satom-scheduler drives the job every 3 seconds. The job does not run as a thread in the web, because the change itself restarts the web and the scheduler. All of its state is in the job file, so it continues where it stopped after those restarts. The peer is still asked only after this node reports success. A failure, rollback, refusal or an unreachable peer ends the job as an error that names the node. The job is never marked successful while the two nodes differ.
            • The peer is never asked twice. If the driver stops while asking, the job fails with "unknown whether the peer received the change". A request the updater does not pick up within 30 minutes, or a job that nothing has advanced for 15 minutes, also fails with the reason.
            • Reopening Settings shows a change that is still running. The /settings/library-pip/peers endpoint, used only by the old browser step, is gone.

            Fixed — a psycopg upgrade from the Libraries card took both HA nodes down; the peer now waits for local success (2026-10-15)

            • Extras were dropped. The card upgraded the bare package name, so psycopg moved to 3.3.6 while psycopg-binary stayed at 3.3.4. Its C wait_c() rejects the new timeout= keyword, so every worker died on its first database connection (the import smoke test passed because importing does not connect). The install, the auto-rollback and the requirements.txt bump now keep the extras pinned there (psycopg[binary]). The bump also no longer appends a second, extras-less line beside an existing name[extra]== pin.
            • Both nodes restarted together. With "also the peer" ticked, the peer was asked at the same moment, so the bad upgrade took a1 and a2 down together for ~100 s until each runner rolled back. The peer is now asked only after this node reports success for that exact package and version. A failed or rolled-back change never reaches it, and the server refuses the peer step otherwise.

            Fixed — the Libraries card no longer reports "status poll failed" while its own upgrade restarts the web (2026-10-15)

            • Upgrading a package from Settings → Libraries restarts satom.service, so the browser's status poll got a 502 for a few seconds. The card gave up on the first failed poll and printed "(status poll failed)", although the upgrade went on to succeed (seen on SQLAlchemy 2.0.52 → 2.1.4). It now shows "service restarting as part of the update — reconnecting…" and keeps polling for up to 3 minutes, like the Software Update page; after that it points to Software Update → Recent updates.

            Added — Certificate Manager: a CSR for another CA, importing certificates, staged rotation and a revocation register (2026-10-15)

            • A CSR for another CA. "Generate CSR" makes the key and the CSR in SATOM. The key never leaves it. The certificate waits as awaiting signature until the signed certificate is imported. Its page shows the round trip: download (or copy) the CSR, then paste or upload what the CA returned. The import is refused unless the public key is the stored key and every requested SAN is present. A PKCS#12 or a pasted key is refused for such a request, because it would bring a different key (operator request: "create a CSR so that another instance signs it, import it, store it with its key and use it in the Cert Manager").
            • Import a certificate + key made outside SATOM, as PEM or PKCS#12. The key is stored encrypted and marked as generated outside SATOM. Per the operator, PKCS#12 is accepted only when the CSR was made outside SATOM.
            • Staged rotation instead of an in-place replacement. A renewal is issued and deployed N days before expiry and takes over the bindings N days later, so issuing and switching do not happen at the same moment and cut connections (operator request: "it should not be swapped the moment it is renewed"). The old certificate stays on the device for a one-click Roll back, leaves the device N days after the swap, and leaves SATOM N days after that; the record (serial, dates, timeline) stays. The four windows are defaults in Settings and can be set per certificate. A swap delay that would land after the old certificate expires is refused. With auto-renew, certificates from the configured CA renew themselves. For another CA a new CSR is generated and the operator is notified. Imported certificates are notified only.
            • Row buttons: renew or generate a new CSR now, download the CSR, import the signed certificate, deploy, swap now, roll back, revoke and delete, each with a confirmation. Each row also shows its next step and when.
            • Generic revocation and a revocation register. Revoking runs the revoke command of whichever CA is configured. When SATOM cannot revoke (no command, or a certificate from another CA), the certificate is marked revoked and the register keeps it pending at the CA until someone confirms it. The register keeps serial, fingerprint, reason, who and result, and outlives a deleted record. A certificate in use is not revoked unless the operator says so (a compromised key). A superseded certificate is revoked as it leaves the device, never while it still serves.
            • Delete is refused while the certificate is bound or its bindings cannot be read. It can revoke first and take the certificate off the device first.
            • Settings → Certificate Manager → Lifecycle policy now holds the default windows. The old "revoke grace" is gone: revocation follows removal from the device. The sweep's dry run now also lists the revocations it would make.

            Changed — API tokens: every non-destructive action has a capability; grouped checkbox pickers (2026-10-15)

            • Six new capabilities cover the rest of the non-destructive catalog: cert_renew (the three Cert Manager renewals), monitoring (deep-monitor sweep, metrics scrape, monitoring report), sentinel (correlate, baselines, CVE mirror, blocklist feed publish), feeds (signature freshness, knowledge packs, WAF artifact index), api_library (endpoint evidence, CLI schema, schema watch) and netbox (NetBox reconcile). Before, these 16 actions had no capability: only a token owned by a user administrator, with no capability ticked, could run them, so no token could be limited to "monitoring only" (operator request: "add more actions"). They are explicit: a token with no capability ticked keeps the old rule for them, so no token issued earlier gained anything. A test now fails when a non-destructive catalog action has no capability. Destructive actions stay unreachable through the API.
            • Capabilities and AppID scope are dropdowns with checkboxes, in the create form and in every Edit dialog (operator request: "put them in a select where the user picks with checkboxes"). Capabilities are grouped (server policies, certificates, maintenance & reports, monitoring & security, feeds & integrations, and the always-explicit object writes), each with its description and an "explicit" badge where an empty list does not grant it. The AppID picker has a filter box. The button lists what is ticked. The Ctrl-click lists are gone. Descriptions and groups now live in the model, next to the capabilities, instead of in the template.
            • docs/api_v1.md gains the capability → action table.

            Fixed — a release that adds a table no longer takes the web down at boot; one FortiWeb's signature alert no longer silences another's (2026-10-15)

            • Workers no longer race on a new table. The four web workers each ran the schema bootstrap at the same time. When a release added a table, two of them sent the same CREATE TABLE, and the one that lost exited. Gunicorn then stopped the whole web service until systemd restarted it (a1, 2026-10-14 10:14, table diag_catalogs). The bootstrap now runs one worker at a time behind a Postgres advisory lock. The wait is bounded at 120 s; after that the worker boots unlocked, as before, and logs that it did.
            • Each FortiWeb has its own signature alert key. Every "Signature DB stale" and "version unreadable" finding used the same key. So one device's cooldown silenced the alert for a different device for six hours. The key now carries the appliance id, as the device-health findings already did.

            Changed — every device can be named on a change request, FortiGate included (2026-10-15)

            • A change request can name a device of any product. The device list used to hold only the products some automated action runs on. No automated action runs on FortiGate, so a FortiGate could not be named on any change, not even a documentary one done by hand (cabling, a PSU swap), and Change types could not offer a type for it. The list now holds every product with an active ADOM (operator request: "make every device able to enter the change request").
            • Automated types still run only on their own products. Choosing one now greys out and unticks the devices it does not run on (e.g. FortiGate for a reboot). The server keeps refusing the mismatch, as before. Documentary types with no product declared keep every device.
            • Change types → Add a change type offers FortiGate under "Offered for".
            • New documentary type "Manual change (performed by hand)", offered for every product. Production had no documentary type, so a FortiGate could be listed on a change request with no type to raise it with (operator confirmed the recommendation). SATOM executes nothing for it: the change request records scope, window, approval and outcome, and its document has its own text in English and German, not the generic "Action without a profile". It is created once at start-up as an ordinary change type, so an administrator can reword, hide or delete it, and a deleted one is not recreated.

            Added — Certificate Manager signs with a CA held in an OPNsense firewall (2026-10-15)

            • New signer scripts/opnsense_ca_signer.py for the ADCS command template. It sends the CSR to OPNsense's Sign CSR action (System › Trust) and writes the signed certificate back (operator request: "create a trust with the firewall's CA and configure it, I want to see how the whole process works"). The private key never leaves SATOM. The API key only needs the System: Certificate Manager privilege. The firewall is identified by a public-key pin, which is checked before any credential is sent. pin prints the value to compare.
            • OPNsense drops the CSR's subjectAltName when it signs, so the signer sends the SANs separately, one per line, because OPNsense rejects a comma-separated list. Without them, browsers and curl reject the certificate.
            • The CA secret now also reaches the signer as $SATOM_CA_SECRET (ADCS submit and revoke). A template can leave out {password} and keep the secret out of /proc/<pid>/cmdline. The OPNsense signer refuses a secret on its command line.

            Fixed — pages that only worked after a refresh; Database relationships; Change types; firmware platform (2026-10-15)

            • Pages opened from the menu now work without a refresh. Turbo Drive re-inserts a page's scripts on every link visit, and the inline code ran before the external file it calls had loaded. After a click, the Database diagram stayed empty ("initERDiagram is not a function"), the Python Console "Browse examples" button did nothing and its Run button was never wired, the Query builder opened with no tables ("Related tables" empty), and Lua Studio → New, Plugin Studio → New and Naming threw the same error. Every page worked after a full reload. turbo-boot.js now runs an inline script only after the external scripts above it have loaded, the order a full load uses. Measured in Chromium on 43 pages: 5 broken before, 0 after, no new errors (operator request: "for the diagram to show I have to refresh the page"; "the examples button does not work"; "in the Query builder Related tables comes up empty").
            • Database: relationships the schema implies are drawn. All 123 tables were already in the diagram, but 48 showed as unconnected because history tables keep appliance_id and similar columns without a foreign key, on purpose: their rows outlive the appliance. An integer <name>_id column now links to the table with that name (singular or plural) whose primary key is id, exact match only (24 relationships). They are drawn dashed, counted apart ("78 foreign keys · 24 inferred"), labelled in the list view, and the Query builder can join on them.
            • The SQL console was already read-only; checked live. DELETE, UPDATE, a data-modifying CTE, two statements, SELECT … FOR UPDATE and set_config are all refused before they run, and the query runs in a read-only, rolled-back transaction under a role that can only SELECT.
            • Change types: aligned form and tables, and real names for four types. The "Add a change type" form had each field at a different height. It now has one row (Key, Name, Written in) and one row of checkboxes for "Offered for", which replace the Ctrl-click list. Both tables share one column grid. HA failover and the three Cert Manager renewals showed "Action without a profile" as their name and printed the generic change document: they now have their own profile in English and German. A test pins every operator action to a profile and to its catalogue label. It also caught the lifecycle sweep's label drifting from the catalogue.
            • Firmware: Hardware or VM is detected from the file name. Fortinet's naming carries it (FWB_KVM-…, FGT_VM64_KVM-… = VM; FWB_1000E-…, FGT_60F-… = hardware). The upload form fills the Platform field, and the hypervisor for install images, when you choose the file and says it was detected. The server applies the same rule to uploads and backup-server pulls. A platform the operator picked is never overruled, and a name that does not say stays "Any". Matching an image to an appliance now reads the appliance's probed hardware type; before, it guessed from the model string (operator request: "firmware should detect directly whether it is HW or VM").

            Changed — Automations regrouped: operator work in Automation, SATOM's own in Administrator; schema pages under API (2026-10-14)

            • System Automations moved to Administrator → System, in every ADOM. These are SATOM's own automations: syncs, backups, probe and metrics sweeps, Sentinel, and feed refreshes. Automation keeps Automations, the work on the fleet's services that operators schedule (operator request: "System Automations are SATOM's own, so they move to Administrator; Automations are what keeps the services on the Forti devices working").
            • Operator actions moved from System Automations to Automations: upgrade preparation, firmware upgrade, reboot, HA failover, the three certificate renewals, the certificate lifecycle sweep and custom REST. Existing rows moved with their action. Operators (config_write) can now schedule them. The dangerous ones still run only bound to an approved Change Request inside its window, and approving a change is an administrator's step. Certificate lifecycle and custom REST now also require an approved Change Request. The form says so when one of these actions is picked. Automations is now live in the FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator ADOMs too. The certificate renewals are now also offered as Change Request types.
            • System automations create themselves. When a node gets its first device, SATOM creates the default set (the same plan as satom execute seed actions), and the "Appliance created" message counts them. This happens only while the node has no system automation at all. A node that has one keeps exactly what its administrator left.
            • Schema builds and Build compatibility moved to the API sub-menu of Automation (operator request: "put Schema builds and Build compatibility into API"). Global now has an API sub-menu holding those two pages. A profile without config_write finds the API menu as its own group in a device ADOM, and inside the Global block in Global.
            • Security: a scheduled row runs only under its own Change Request. The executor now checks that the bound change covers the row: same action, and only devices the change names. Before, any row carrying an approved change's id ran inside that change's window. Since operators can now edit these rows, that would have let one reboot every device under someone else's approved upgrade. The form can no longer set or remove a binding. Only the change's Schedule button writes it.
            • Fixed: a change naming no device can no longer be scheduled. Its row carried an empty target list, which the executor reads as the whole fleet. An approved reboot naming nothing would have rebooted every appliance. Such a change can still be saved and read.
            • Links that sent operators to the page they cannot open now go to the page that owns the row: the upgrade flow's rollout button and the "automation failing" alert.

            Changed — Global draws Automation like the device ADOMs; Administrator in alphabetical sections (2026-10-14)

            • Automation in the Global ADOM is a sub-menu of the Global block, above Jobs. This is the same place it has inside Operations in the device ADOMs (operator request: "in Global also put Automation the way it is in the other ADOMs"). Entries and permissions are unchanged.
            • Administrator is grouped into sections: Access, Change Management, Devices, Objects, Studio and System. Sections and the entries inside each one are sorted alphabetically (operator request: "group the Administrator section and sort the groups and the entries of each group alphabetically"). The sort uses the labels in the console's language, so the order is alphabetical in German, Spanish, French and Italian too, ignoring case and accents. A section with no entry the profile may open is not drawn. In the device ADOMs, Python Console moved into Administrator → Studio. No entry changed its permission. A profile without the administrator role still sees the Process entry on its own.

            Changed — Certificate Manager in every ADOM (2026-10-14)

            • Certificate Manager is now in every device ADOM, in Operations › Automation, as it already was in the Global ADOM's Automation group (operator request: "put Certificate Manager in every ADOM inside Operations, as it is"). It is live in FortiWeb and FortiADC and lists only that ADOM's devices. In FortiGate, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator it is drawn disabled with the reason: SATOM reads and deploys certificates on FortiWeb and FortiADC only. It still requires the administrator role.
            • Fixed: Global's Scan devices no longer sends FortiWeb calls to other products. The Global device list included FortiGate, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator. The scan sent them FortiWeb REST and SSH calls, then reported them as unreachable. The device lists, the scans and the sidebar now read one list of supported kinds.

            Fixed — proxyd no longer reported as "NOT running" when it is at 100 % CPU (2026-10-14)

            • The proxyd deep monitor read a daemon at full CPU as a dead one. In diagnose system top the CPU-core and %CPU columns run together when a process reaches 100 % (0100.0). That row did not match the parser, proxyd disappeared from the process list and the probe went critical with "proxyd is NOT running" — four times on a lab FortiWeb 7.6.8 while the same PID kept running. The parser now reads the run-together form. As a second guard, a proxyd row that is present but cannot be read grades as an error (a parser gap), never as an absent daemon.

            Fixed — adding a device no longer leaves it unmonitored or buried in false alerts (2026-10-14)

            • Discover no longer creates probes that can only fail. Published policies now dials each new front end once before creating its probe. A VIP that SATOM cannot connect to (connect timeout, refused, TLS failure before a session, or a target the network guard refuses) gets its probe disabled, with the reason in its last result. The discovery message counts these probes. Before this change they were created enabled and stayed critical forever: on a lab FortiWeb, 49 of 55 deep monitors were red against 172.0.0.x VIPs that nothing routed to, while CPU, memory and proxyd were healthy, and Device health showed the device as critical. A front end that connects but answers badly is still created enabled. Disabled policies are not dialled.
            • Every way of adding a device now creates its baseline probes. Devices added through the REST API (POST /api/appliances) or onboarded by a provisioning run got scrape targets but no thresholds, so Device health showed "no deep monitors configured" until someone pressed Discover. Both paths now use the same provisioning step as the web form. The 3-minute Collection sweep also gives the baseline to any device that has no probe at all, which covers rows inserted by imports or scripts. It does not re-create a probe that was deleted on a provisioned device. A test fails if any function that creates an appliance skips provisioning.
            • The infra collector works on a mapped device and no longer fails on an unmapped one. It built the hypervisor VM reference without two required fields, so it raised an error on every device mapped to its VM. Nobody had noticed because no device had been mapped until now. It also gave every FortiWeb and FortiADC an infra target that failed every 3 minutes until the device was mapped, and a hardware appliance can never be mapped. The target is now created only once the topology mapping is complete, and the Collection sweep adds it on the next pass after the mapping is saved. A read-only Proxmox API token (role PVEAuditor) is enough for this collector.
            • Device health says when it cuts the list of failing probes: "49/55 probes alerting: a, b, c, d (+45 more)" instead of four names that read as the whole list.

            Fixed — the manual deploy migrates the database schema (2026-10-14)

            • satom execute restart-all runs flask db upgrade on a primary when the schema is behind the newest migration, before the stack restarts. Only the update runner and the container image migrated; the deploy by git pull + restart-all never did. Boot-time table creation added the new tables and columns, so nothing failed, but a1's recorded schema version stayed at sigidx01 under four newer revisions (sshpw01, tplbind01, netarch01, diagbat01). A migration that transforms data would have been skipped in silence. A standby is skipped: it follows the primary by replication.
            • satom get system health shows the schema version and warns when it is behind head, with the command that fixes it.

            Added — Diagnostic Battery per ADOM; Diagnose Log Collection in every device ADOM (2026-10-14)

            • Security: the console accepted any diagnose command. The read-only gate (ssh_ops.assert_readonly) allowed every line starting with diagnose or diag, so the appliance SSH Console and the Log Collection custom-commands box would send diagnose debug kernel sysrq command crash, diagnose ha failover … or diagnose sys kill …. Every diagnose statement is now checked by name and refused when a word changes the device: kill, clear, reset, delete, failover, sysrq/crash, enable/disable, set, format, fsck, rmmod and similar, plus level on its own (FortiGate diagnose ip router ospf level error sets a debug level). Abbreviations count, because the CLI completes them: diag sys kil 11 1 reads as kill. get and show are unchanged.
            • New page: Administrator → Diagnostic Battery (user_manage), in each device ADOM (FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiGate, FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator). An administrator chooses the commands that make up the ADOM's battery. Commands can be ticked from a tree discovered on a real device of the ADOM or typed by hand. Save keeps the order of the commands already in the battery, and Reset to default returns to the product default. The Global ADOM shows a read-only summary of the five batteries.
            • Discovery reads the device's own diagnose tree. It types <path> ? on the device CLI over SSH, walks the tree and stores the result per product and firmware build. Each node is classified by its name and by the device's description of it before it is asked, and a refused node is never asked. Measured in the lab: FortiGate 8.0.1, 3,015 nodes in about ten minutes; FortiAnalyzer 7.6.7, 612; FortiADC 8.0.4, 598. FortiWeb and FortiADC close the SSH session when ? follows a node with exactly one child (diagnose hardware cpu), so such a node is read by TAB completion on a new session. When FortiAuthenticator does not answer a ?, the node is asked again. Values the CLI lists under an argument (FortiWeb lists every policy under <policy name>) are kept as examples of the argument, not walked. A discovery whose process died (a restart) is shown as interrupted instead of blocking new discoveries for 70 minutes. On FortiWeb, ? after some leaves runs the (read-only) command, so the page recommends running discovery on a lab unit or in a maintenance window.
            • The battery rule. A battery refuses state-changing commands by name, by the device's description of the command or of any parent ("Kill a process.", "set/get debug level…", "Generate one system info log file every 2 minutes."), and, because a battery runs unattended, commands that never return, flood the session or send traffic (top, sniffer, debug flow, ping, traceroute, test). The rule is checked when the battery is saved and again before each run.
            • Diagnose Log Collection moves to Operations › Troubleshooting in all five device ADOMs; until now it was a FortiWeb-only entry under Operations. It runs the active ADOM's battery, which is listed read-only on the page, with a link to the editor for administrators. If a device's build does not have a command (according to that build's discovery), the command is skipped and the report says SKIPPED: not present in <build>. The same happens when the build lists the command as a branch without <Enter>, which needs a subcommand there: FortiADC 7.6.7 and 8.0.4 answer diagnose hardware get sysinfo on its own with "Incorrect number of parameters". Output such as "Command fail" or "Parsing error" is tagged [not available on this build]. The custom box follows the battery rule. The FortiWeb default battery has 28 commands: diagnose debug proxy log 3 is gone. It printed nothing on 7.6.8 or 8.0.6, and its parent is described as set/get, meaning the trailing number sets a debug level. The other four products start from defaults that ran on the lab devices: neither FortiGate 8.0.1 nor FortiAnalyzer 7.6.7 has diagnose debug crashlog read (FortiGate uses diagnose debug crashlog get), and FortiADC uses the sysinfo/deviceinfo leaves (cpu, memory, nic).
            • Appliances: "SSH user, if different from the API user". A FortiGate registered with a REST api-user cannot open SSH with that user. Log collection now logs in with the separate SSH user and the separate SSH password. Before this it sent the API password, which failed on FortiAuthenticator, whose REST key SSH refuses.
            • Processes: the "Collect diagnostic logs" step runs the device's own battery. It ran FortiWeb's battery on every product. It now runs the battery of the device's ADOM, planned against its build exactly like Diagnose Log Collection, and its result says how many commands ran and how many were skipped.
            • Fixed: the one-at-a-time guards of log collection and rediscovery read their start time in local time. The stamp is UTC, so on a node whose clock is not UTC a running collection looked hours older (UTC+N) or younger (UTC−N) than it was, and a second run could start beside it. Nodes on UTC, such as the reference pair, were not affected.
            • Migration diagbat01: tables diag_catalogs and diag_batteries, and the column appliances.ssh_username.

            Security — the operator CLI no longer runs the app tree as root (2026-10-14)

            • satom under sudo drops to the service account before executing anything from /opt/satom. Diagnostics ran git status as root inside the repository, which executes what the service account's .git/config names (core.fsmonitor, measured); every venv snippet (_app_call: update/promote enqueue, backups, scheduler and device actions, the automatic backup db of execute update package), flask one-shots, diagnose python and the support bundle ran the venv python or pip as root; execute reinstall venv ran pip install -r requirements.txt as root and then chowned the result recursively, following symlinks. All of these now run as the service account (runuser -m -u, or setpriv to the tree's uid when it has no name); the venv is built as that account and nothing is chowned afterwards. A test fails on any git/venv/flask/pip command the CLI builds without the drop.
            • Root no longer writes or chowns through the service account's directories. execute repair permissions chowned whatever a symlink in data/ pointed to (e.g. /etc/shadow) to the service account; it now walks by directory fd, never follows a link and skips hard-linked files. Update packages and API packs are staged in data/ by a child that already dropped privileges (execute update fetch downloads into a root-private directory first), queue files are created exclusively and without following links, and every remaining chown is follow_symlinks=False.

            Security — signed releases, node request signing, console hardening (2026-10-14)

            • Signed-release enforcement is activatable without blocking HA. With a root-owned trust anchor (/etc/satom/release-trust.allowed_signers, or a single key at …/release-trust.pub), root-side content — unit files, the install-*.sh scripts, the operator CLI and the runner copies — comes from the newest signed release: the target itself, or its signed ancestor when deploy/ is identical. An unsigned change to deploy/ no longer refuses the update: the application updates and only the root-side refresh is held, shown as a warning, so the standby keeps converging. New satom execute sign-release (dry run by default; signs on the primary with a root-only key and pushes) and satom get release trust; the satom execute reinstall verbs are gated the same way. Root now verifies inside a root-only mirror and never runs git inside the service account's repository (the first version ran that repository's configured programs as root), and the .pub single-key anchor now works. With no anchor, behaviour is unchanged.
            • Node-to-node requests are HMAC-signed. Every peer request carries X-SATOM-Node-Ts + X-SATOM-Node-Sig (HMAC-SHA256 over method, path+query, timestamp and body hash, keyed with the node identity key). The raw key never crosses the wire, signatures older than 120 s are refused, and the static X-FM-Node-Key header is no longer accepted. The peer certificate must now verify (system trust store or internal CA): an untrusted certificate is refused with a logged reason instead of silently downgrading. Emergency override: SATOM_PEER_TLS_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED=1. Both nodes must run this release; expect about a minute of "not authenticated" peer views while the standby catches up, and keep both clocks NTP-synchronised.
            • The database console runs under a dedicated read-only role. The console, report widgets and plugin datasets now run every query as satom_console_ro: no monitoring privileges, no access to the credential tables or credential columns (list columns explicitly instead of SELECT * on appliances or managed certificates), and refused outright when the role is not provisioned — never a fallback to the application role. Provisioned by the installer and on update by deploy/install-console-role.sh (primary only; the standby gets it by replication).
            • The metrics store's admin endpoints require keys (delete, snapshot, force-merge, reload, flags, pprof…), generated into a root-only /etc/satom/metrics-auth.env by install-metrics-store.sh; the application only holds the snapshot key it needs.
            • The Device Console gate reads Fortinet abbreviations the way the CLI does. Any prefix — exe fa, exe reb, set passw, quoted keywords, ? help keys — is classified as forbidden or needs acknowledgement (before, exe fa sent a factory reset as an ordinary line). Transcripts and TAC bundles redact abbreviated and compound secret attributes.
            • Scout checks a typed Published host by host and port against the appliance inventory, not by host alone.

            Fixed — monitoring and source of truth (2026-10-14)

            • FortiAnalyzer CPU and memory probes read the 7.6 get system performance block layout: {device} graded "error" on every sample and stayed "degraded". Memory is physical RAM, like FortiWeb/FortiADC.
            • The FortiADC/FortiAnalyzer box-metrics scrape writes its CPU and memory series: it read keys the parser never produced, so both were always empty.
            • The source-of-truth identity drops FortiAnalyzer's per-read salted ["ENC", …] secrets as a backstop to the sweep scrub, so an unchanged box can never again mint an hourly version and drift alert. The "ENC …" strings FortiWeb/FortiADC store are still compared.
            • Config-drift alerting no longer mutes a device named {device} by default; alerts.drift_exclude is empty unless the operator sets it.
            • The HA datasync no longer copies the integration-hook queue (data/integrations/queue/, claimed/) to the standby. The hook runner is meant to be enabled on both nodes; with the queue replicated, the standby would have run every pending hook a second time, which is why it had been left disabled there (and hooks would not have run after a failover).

            Changed — FortiADC API library (2026-10-14)

            • REST↔CLI field renames measured value by value on {device} (7.6.7, 115) and {device} (8.0.4, 85) are now one field under the REST name (e.g. pool = load-balance-pool), so they no longer read "unverified on this build"; 7.6.7 goes from 967 to 1,082 fields "both". A build that was not measured gets no renames.
            • The schema harvest runs a read-only REST shape probe on FortiADC: top-level objects and child tables by ?pkey=. A 404 at a child path is not recorded as absent, because FortiADC serves some children only inside the parent row.

            Changed — navigation labels (2026-10-14)

            • Log Collection is now Diagnose Log Collection (menu, page title, translations). Its battery lost two commands that never returned data on FortiWeb 7.6.8 or 8.0.6: diagnose hardware harddisk on its own (it only prints "you must specify cmd"; its list, info, health, errors and attributes sub-commands stay) and diagnose system ha export-eventlog (it needs parameters). diagnose hardware cpu printed nothing on both builds and is now diagnose hardware cpu list, which answers. The firmware-flash before/after battery reuses the same list.
            • The Fleet group is gone; Operations is the first group of every device ADOM. It opens with the fleet pages and then holds Device Backups, Log Collection and Import Backup (and Template Library for profiles outside Administrator). The device's own menu now follows Operations. The Global ADOM keeps its Global block and has no Operations group.
            • The API console is a sub-menu of Automation (Automation › API › Registry & console) instead of a group of its own. A profile that may open the console (registry.view) but cannot see Automation (no config_write) keeps the standalone API group, so no profile loses the page and none sees it twice. Every entry keeps its own permission: the menu moved, access did not change.
            • Automation is the last entry of Operations in every device ADOM: a sub-menu (Operations › Automation, with Automation › API inside it) instead of a group of its own. The Global ADOM, which has no Operations group, keeps Automation as a group. Entries and permissions are unchanged. The API console link now carries its ADOM (?_adom=) like the other Automation entries, so a link opened in a new tab lands in the right ADOM.
            • Troubleshooting (under Operations in the device ADOMs, in the Global block in Global) holds Backend Reachability, Config Compare, Path Diagnostics and Scout; the separate Troubleshooting entries under Operations and the flat entries in the Global list are gone. The fleet pages run Dashboard (where an ADOM has one), Calendar, Architecture, Service Diagram, Monitoring, Search, DNS Lookup, Troubleshooting, then Fleet Objects and WAF (FortiWeb and FortiADC ADOMs only) and Jobs last.
            • The fault-localisation ladder formerly called "Scout" is labelled Path Diagnostics; the AI assistant formerly called "AI Advisor" is labelled Scout; the firmware release-notes reviewer formerly shown as "Scout" is the Upgrade Advisory, and when it is unavailable it says Path Diagnostics must be switched on in Settings → Path Diagnostics — the switch it actually uses. Menu, page titles, settings panes and messages; URLs and bookmarks are unchanged.
            • In the FortiGate, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator ADOMs, Operations › Troubleshooting holds Scout only: Backend Reachability, Config Compare and Path Diagnostics work on FortiWeb and FortiADC objects and are no longer listed there. The pages still open by URL.
            • The Fleet health sub-menu is gone. Device health is a direct entry of Monitoring in every ADOM (in a device ADOM the sub-menu held nothing else); in Global, SATOM health follows it as a direct entry. Pages, URLs and permissions are unchanged.

            Changed — ADOM Search searches each ADOM's own configuration (2026-10-14)

            • The Search page is titled ADOM Search (it was "Global Search") and searches the configuration SATOM last synced from the appliances of the active ADOM — FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator or FortiAnalyzer, or all of them in the Global ADOM. It used to query five FortiWeb REST paths live and send them to every device that was not a FortiADC, so a FortiAuthenticator RADIUS client, a FortiGate address or a FortiAnalyzer managed device was never found.
            • Every synced collection is searched, not a fixed list. Each match shows the section, type, object (with its parent object for sub-table rows), field and value, and each appliance shows when its configuration was last synced. An appliance with no synced configuration is named as not searched.
            • The Object Type filter is replaced by Section, listing the sections the ADOM's appliances actually have. The subtitle, placeholder and tips are specific to each ADOM.
            • Passwords, keys, pre-shared secrets and ENC values are never matched or shown, so the search cannot be used to guess a secret.
            • The top-bar search button is also shown in the FortiAnalyzer ADOM. Menu entry, URL and bookmarks are unchanged.

            Security — infrastructure hardening (2026-10-13 internal code audit)

            • Node-to-node transport is HTTPS-only and certificate-verified. The peer probes between the two HA nodes no longer fall back to plain HTTP, so the shared identity key can never cross the wire in cleartext, and the peer's TLS certificate is now validated against the system trust store (the public fleet wildcard) or the internal CA. A genuinely untrusted certificate still connects, but over encrypted TLS and with a logged warning, so the health dashboards never break.
            • HSTS (Strict-Transport-Security) is now sent on every response, scoped to the node's own host (no includeSubDomains/preload, so sibling fleet services are unaffected).
            • The integration-hook sandbox can no longer read the secret files. The unprivileged hook runner masks /opt/satom/.env, the internal-CA key under pki/ and the HA key under .ssh/, and hides other processes, so a hook cannot reach the Fernet key or database URL on disk.

            Security — second round of the 2026-10-13 internal code audit

            Accounts and sign-in - A password-reset link is now single-use: it is tied to the current password and stops working the moment the password changes. - A TOTP code can no longer be used twice inside its time window. - The sign-in page no longer reveals that an account is disabled or awaiting approval before the password is checked, and an unknown username now takes the same time as a real one. - Setting a recovery email, starting 2FA setup, enabling 2FA and regenerating backup codes now require the current password (and, when 2FA is already on, a current code), the same proof disabling 2FA already asked for. Enabling 2FA refuses to overwrite an authenticator that is already set up. The Settings → Security forms carry the extra fields.

            Directory sign-in - An account imported from one directory can only be signed into through that same directory. A directory that merely shares the account name can no longer take it over, and login never rewrites an existing account's source. - The Active Directory membership check escapes the name and prefers the exact signed-in identity, so a like-named account in another domain cannot pass.

            Authorization - The read-write Device Console now requires the device-apply permission, not any minor edit permission. - Turning off an appliance's TLS verification now requires the password again, like changing its host. - A template cannot be approved by its own author. - CLI-coverage evidence and dumps from a device in maintenance mode are hidden from users who may not see that device. - A non-admin can no longer schedule or run an automation against a device hidden from them, and their "all targets" no longer reaches hidden devices.

            Stored markup - Values that come from a managed appliance or from another user (device and host names, log lines, policy and signature names, error text) are escaped before being placed in the page, on the Logs, Settings, Exceptions, Object editor, Server-Policy wizard, FortiAnalyzer and analysis views.

            Security — fixes from the 2026-10-13 internal code audit

            Appliance command injection - Certificate import (and the certificate carry between appliances) accepted a backslash inside a PEM or passphrase. The device CLI treats \ as an escape inside a quoted value, so a key ending in \ kept the quote open and the lines after it ran as raw configuration commands, for example creating an administrator. PEM values are now rebuilt from their BEGIN/base64/END lines only, and ", \ and control characters are refused in PEMs and passphrases. A hostile source appliance can no longer inject into the destination during a carry. - The read-only console gates (console, CLI coverage live read, probe and schema gates) passed control characters to the interactive shell, where backspace or Ctrl-U erase the show and leave a write. Every gate now refuses control characters. The write console also classifies abbreviated verbs (exe factoryres, exec reboot) the way the full words are classified.

            Authorization - Changing an appliance's host, port, username or platform kept its stored password, so the next sync sent the device credentials to the new endpoint. The edit form and PUT /api/appliances/<id> now require the password to be entered again for such a change, and the SSH password too when the row holds a separate one. - A user with users.manage or profiles.manage could grant themselves any permission: assign themselves (or create) a wider profile, add keys to the profile they are assigned to, or reset the password or 2FA of a more privileged account. Each of these is now refused unless the actor already holds every permission involved. - An API token owned by a non-admin could run System Automations and actions with no capability mapping (system backup, git bundle, certificate issuing…). These now need an owner with user management, as in the browser.

            Server-side requests - Network Architecture probes, monitor HTTPS probes and process http_check steps could reach the node's own loopback services, including the metrics store, which has no authentication, and cloud metadata addresses. They now go through the target guard, resolve the name once and connect to that address. The node's internal ports (5432, 8000, 8428) are refused in every mode, including the Transaction Tracer, whose inventory mode now checks the port as well as the host. - The DNS tool and process DNS checks refused nothing that starts with -, so an entry such as -f<file> made dig read a local file. Names and servers are now validated.

            Sign-in and sessions - The post-login redirect accepted /<tab>/host, which browsers follow to another site. It now accepts local paths only. - The remember-me cookie is now Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax and lasts 14 days (it was not Secure and lasted 365 days). - 2FA: the half-signed-in state expires after 5 minutes, wrong codes count toward the account lockout and are audited (login.2fa_fail), and a correct password no longer resets the failure count before the code is checked. - Any Authorization: Bearer header switched the idle session lock off for a cookie session. Only the API is exempt now.

            Unauthenticated endpoints - /healthz without the inter-node identity key now answers only ok and peer_authenticated. The revision, host statistics and database detail are reserved for the peer node. /healthz/primary no longer returns database error text, and /healthz/backups, /healthz/cert-renewals and /healthz/reconciler answer 403 without the key. An HA pair needs the identity key configured for its peer views (it is, on every pair that shows the encrypted channel as configured).

            Other hardening - The self-update runner (root) validates the request id, the branch and the target, rejects unknown request kinds, and writes status, library and requirements files without following symbolic links. Promote runs the root-owned /usr/local/sbin/satom-promote.sh, never the copy in the application tree; a node without it refuses promote until install-runner.sh is run. Package extraction refuses links already on disk and archives over 2 GiB unpacked. - Regex Lab evaluates each pattern in a separate process killed after 2 seconds, so a catastrophic pattern can no longer hold a web worker. - The read-only SQL console refuses functions that read tables by name inside a string (query_to_xml and the other *_to_xml functions), file and large-object functions, and backend signalling. - Import Backup caps decompressed sizes and no longer writes outside its folder for a device named ..; the flash report no longer creates a folder for any job id it is asked to read.

            Fixed — FortiADC live state was reported as configuration drift

            • A FortiADC returns the live state of some objects inside their configuration rows: a virtual server's or pool's availability (HEALTHY, DEAD …), an interface's availability, and a certificate's status (OK, Expired). Each flip minted a configuration version and raised Config drift … it came from the device side. On the lab box {device} every version since 2026-10-12 — four versions and 20 drift alerts — differed in nothing else, and the device swung back to an earlier version when the virtual server recovered.
            • These fields are no longer part of a configuration version. The rule is keyed by table: status stays configuration in every other FortiADC table, and the configured state next to each stripped field (the virtual server's enable/disable/maintain, the certificate's validity dates) still mints a version when it changes. Existing histories are re-keyed in place on the next sync; it creates no version and no alert.

            Fixed — satom get alerts status said "ok" while every alert email was refused

            • The status judged the settings, not delivery. On a1 the settings were complete and the status said ok while the local mail relay answered 454 4.7.1 Relay access denied to every alert from 2026-09-23 onward: 186 refusals, nothing delivered, alerts reached the in-app bell only.
            • The alert engine now keeps the outcome of its last send attempt, and the status shows it under last email and turns bad when that attempt was not delivered.

            Fixed — alert email: Gmail refused every message without a Message-ID; delivered-but-unsigned is now an error

            • SATOM built its messages without Message-ID and Date. A local Postfix added both on the way out, which hid the gap; any other hand-off is refused by Gmail (550 5.7.1 Messages missing a valid Message-ID header). Every message now carries both headers.
            • Delivered is not received. When the local mail server hands mail straight to the recipient's server with no DKIM signature (Postfix with no relayhost and no signing milter), the message passes SPF at most and Gmail, Outlook and others may file it as spam. SATOM now reports that as a deliverability error: a red box on Settings → Email, a second red line under Send test after a successful send, and in satom get alerts status (last email → deliverability: ERROR, status bad). An external SMTP provider, a relayhost or a signing milter clears it.
            • The Send test result box shows the server's reply as text; it used to insert it as HTML.

            Fixed — two sidebar groups named "Automation", and a Process entry lost next to Studio

            • A profile without user management (operator, read-only) saw the Process page in a group of its own labelled Automation, next to the real Automation group: two groups with one name. That group is now labelled Process.
            • In the Global ADOM a custom profile without user management that holds a Studio permission got the Studio group instead of Process, so a page it may open had no menu entry. It now gets both.
